Narrative: The II:8998932 G>A splice-acceptor change in tdp-1 is high impact and likely disrupts TDP-1 RNA binding/splicing function in neurons and glia. TDP-1/TDP-43 orthologs regulate alternative splicing and neuronal RNA metabolism; mis-splicing of transcripts that specify asymmetric division or neuronal fate in AMso could convert the asymmetric AMso division into a symmetric glial division, eliminating the MCM neurons during male maturation [Effect=splice_acceptor_variant&intron_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 40891506, 32531261].
rationale: High-impact splice-acceptor variant likely disrupts tdp-1 function in RNA processing in neurons/glia; mis-splicing of determinants of asymmetric division or glial-to-neuron fate programs could cause AMso to divide symmetrically and fail to produce MCM neurons [Effect=splice_acceptor_variant&intron_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 40891506, 32531261].

Narrative: V:20636314 A>T affects a splice-donor in ttr-13 (transthyretin-like), predicted to be cell-surface localized. Altered secretion or cell-surface signaling from mutant TTR-13 could change the AMso microenvironment or intercellular signals required for a male-specific asymmetric division, biasing AMso to form two glia rather than produce an MCM neuron [Effect=splice_donor_variant&intron_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: High-impact splice-donor variant in a transthyretin-like (ttr) family member predicted at the cell surface could alter secreted/signaling environment of the amphid socket glia; altered extracellular cues during male maturation could bias AMso divisions toward glial fate rather than producing an MCM neuron [Effect=splice_donor_variant&intron_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: A missense variant in sys-1 is a strong mechanistic candidate because SYS-1 is a central effector in the Wnt/β-catenin asymmetry pathway that patterns asymmetric neuroblast divisions. Modulation of SYS-1 activity can directly alter daughter-cell fate choice; a damaging missense could abolish the AMso asymmetric fate cue and result in symmetric glial daughters and absent MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 29962933, 19389360, 21917811].
rationale: sys-1 is a core beta-catenin–type asymmetry pathway effector required for asymmetric neuroblast divisions and fate specification; a missense change in sys-1 could impair the Wnt/beta-catenin asymmetry machinery in the AMso lineage and directly cause symmetric division and loss of the MCM fate [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 29962933, PMID 19389360, PMID 21917811].

Narrative: The missense variant in fem-1 affects a gene needed for male somatic/germ-line sex determination and part of Cullin2 ubiquitin ligase complexes. Disruption of male-specific regulatory programs during sexual maturation could prevent the AMso glia from executing the male-specific asymmetric division that produces MCMs, making fem-1 a plausible candidate for the phenotype [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15082774].
rationale: fem-1 functions in male germ-line and somatic sex determination and is part of ubiquitin ligase complexes that regulate sex-specific development. A missense change could perturb male-specific transcriptional or post-translational programs in AMso during male maturation, preventing the male-specific asymmetric division that generates MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15082774].

Narrative: jmjd-1.2 encodes a histone demethylase that regulates developmental signaling and axon guidance; a missense variant could alter chromatin states controlling expression of fate determinants in AMso. Perturbed expression of genes required for asymmetric division or male-specific differentiation could favor symmetric glial outcomes, causing MCM loss [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 28126843].
rationale: jmjd-1.2 encodes a histone demethylase implicated in regulation of signaling pathways that control neuronal development; chromatin dysregulation can alter expression of fate determinants required for AMso asymmetric division. A missense variant could change epigenetic regulation of genes instructing the glia-to-neuron fate switch [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 28126843].

Narrative: wdr-48 functions with deubiquitinating enzymes to regulate protein stability, including neuronal receptors; a missense change could alter abundance or trafficking of surface proteins that provide polarity or fate signals to AMso. If key polarity or signaling receptors are destabilized, asymmetric division could fail and MCM neurons would be absent [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 24356955, 32587090].
rationale: wdr-48 acts with deubiquitinating enzymes to regulate receptor abundance and protein stability in neurons; a missense change could alter degradation/stability of membrane or signaling proteins in AMso required for asymmetric fate decisions, leading to symmetric glial divisions and absent MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 24356955, PMID 32587090].

Narrative: alg-1 is a core miRNA pathway component (RISC) that times developmental programs in neurons; a missense variant could dysregulate microRNA-mediated repression of factors that promote AMso-to-MCM fate. Timing or level defects in heterochronic/neuronal miRNAs can convert expected asymmetric divisions into symmetric ones, producing two glia instead of an MCM [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 29117550, 23599497].
rationale: alg-1 is a core miRNA pathway component (RISC) that times developmental switches in neurons; a missense change could dysregulate heterochronic or neuron-specifying microRNAs that are necessary for the AMso-to-MCM transition during male maturation, producing fate conversion to glia [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 29117550, PMID 23599497].

Narrative: cdh-1 encodes a cadherin involved in cell–cell adhesion and tissue architecture; a missense alteration could perturb adhesion-mediated polarization or contact-dependent signaling in AMso. Disruption of those cues often changes spindle orientation or fate signaling and can convert asymmetric divisions to symmetric glial outcomes, accounting for missing MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15924262].
rationale: cdh-1 encodes a cadherin involved in cell–cell adhesion; adhesion cues orient divisions and impact fate; a missense alteration could disrupt AMso adhesion or junctional signaling required for asymmetric spindle positioning and fate determination, leading to symmetric AMso daughter outcomes and no MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 15924262].

Narrative: unc-52 (perlecan) is an ECM component that shapes the local niche and can influence cell polarity and division orientation; a missense change could modify the basement membrane near AMso, altering cues required for asymmetric division. ECM-mediated changes in mechanical or signaling context could lead to symmetric AMso divisions and loss of MCM neurons [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 25982673].
rationale: unc-52 (perlecan) is an ECM/basement membrane component that affects cell positioning and dendrite/axon morphogenesis; ECM disruption can alter local niche signals and mechanical cues that direct asymmetric division of socket glia, so a missense variant is a plausible indirect cause of AMso symmetric division and MCM absence [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 25982673].

Narrative: daf-2 (insulin/IGF receptor) modulates neuronal development and systemic signaling; a missense variant may alter signaling balance during male maturation that is required for AMso asymmetric division timing or competence. Altered insulin signaling could therefore contribute indirectly to a failure to produce MCMs from AMso [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 31619788].
rationale: daf-2 encodes the insulin/IGF receptor with roles in neuronal development and signaling; a missense change could shift signaling thresholds during male maturation that control cell fate or timing of division in AMso, biasing toward glial rather than neuronal outcome [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 31619788].

Narrative: rsp-2 is predicted to encode an RNA-binding/splicing factor; a missense variant could change splicing of transcripts important for asymmetric division or neuronal fate in the AMso lineage. Splicing perturbations in fate determinants or polarity proteins can produce symmetric divisions and eliminate neuron production [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: rsp-2 is predicted to be an RNA-binding splicing factor; missense variants can alter alternative splicing of fate determinants in glia. Disruption in splicing control can reasonably alter AMso fate specification leading to loss of MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: gcy-5 encodes a receptor guanylate cyclase in sensory neurons; although primarily chemosensory, altered cGMP signaling in head neurons/glia could perturb intercellular signaling during male maturation. A missense variant could indirectly influence AMso behavior, making gcy-5 a moderate indirect candidate for MCM loss [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 19523832].
rationale: gcy-5 is a receptor guanylate cyclase expressed in neurons and cilia; although primarily sensory, altered gcy-5 signaling could perturb local neuronal–glial signaling during maturation. A missense change could change cGMP-dependent signaling that indirectly influences AMso division orientation or fate [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 19523832].

Narrative: ppat-1 functions in purine biosynthesis; dividing/progenitor cells can be sensitive to nucleotide biosynthesis defects. A missense variant could reduce AMso proliferative fidelity or change division outcome during maturation, indirectly causing absence of MCM neurons [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: ppat-1 functions in purine biosynthesis; metabolic impairment can selectively affect dividing cells or signaling in developing tissues. A missense variant might reduce metabolic support for asymmetric division in AMso, indirectly causing symmetric divisions and MCM loss [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: mrpl-10 is a mitochondrial ribosomal protein required for mitochondrial translation; mitochondrial dysfunction can alter division patterns and cell fate. A missense change may impair AMso energetic/metabolic support during maturation and bias divisions toward symmetric glial outcomes [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: mrpl-10 is a mitochondrial ribosomal protein; mitochondrial dysfunction can alter cell division patterns and fate decisions. A missense change could impair mitochondrial translation in AMso cells at maturation, biasing divisions and causing MCM absence [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: polq-1 encodes polymerase θ involved in DNA repair and gap-filling; defects can increase DNA damage or checkpoint activation during divisions. A missense variant could alter AMso mitoses and indirectly change the balance between symmetric and asymmetric divisions, reducing MCM formation [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: polq-1 encodes DNA polymerase θ involved in repair and gap-filling; defects can increase genomic stress during divisions. A missense change could make AMso divisions error-prone or trigger checkpoints altering division asymmetry, potentially eliminating MCM production [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: tag-325 is predicted to encode a GAP for small GTPases; small GTPase signaling controls spindle orientation and polarity. A missense variant could perturb actin/microtubule dynamics during AMso mitosis and lead to symmetric divisions and absence of MCMs [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: tag-325 is predicted GTPase-activating protein; small GTPase signaling regulates cytoskeleton and spindle orientation. A missense change could perturb spindle positioning during AMso mitosis and convert an asymmetric into a symmetric division, preventing MCM specification [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: irld-66 is an L-domain receptor family member; if expressed in glia or nearby neurons, a missense change could alter reception of extracellular fate cues. Loss or alteration of a pro-neuronal signal during male maturation may bias AMso toward producing two glia rather than an MCM neuron [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: irld-66 encodes a receptor L-domain protein; altered extracellular receptor signaling in AMso could change responsiveness to fate cues. A missense variant might blunt a pro-neuronal signal needed to generate the MCM fate, leaving two glia instead [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: nos-3 is an RNA-binding protein with strong roles in germline but potential RNA regulatory roles elsewhere; a missense variant could have ectopic somatic effects on mRNA stability or translation of cell-fate regulators in AMso. This makes it a low-probability candidate for affecting asymmetric division and MCM production [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: nos-3 is an RNA-binding factor involved mainly in germline processes, but RNA-binding proteins can also influence neuronal fate determinants; a missense change might have ectopic effects in somatic cells that alter fate specification in the AMso lineage [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: imph-1 (mRNA 3'-UTR binding) is implicated in nervous system development; a missense change could alter post-transcriptional control of key fate determinants in AMso. Such regulatory changes could bias AMso divisions away from MCM generation, though direct evidence is lacking [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: imph-1 is an mRNA 3'-UTR binding protein predicted to be involved in nervous system development; missense variants can alter post-transcriptional regulation of fate determinants, plausibly affecting AMso asymmetric outcomes and MCM generation [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: srh-173 is a chemoreceptor family member; changes here are unlikely to directly alter AMso intrinsic fate machinery but may affect sensory input that modulates developmental timing/signaling. Considered an indirect, low-probability candidate for MCM loss [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: srh-173 is a predicted chemoreceptor; while primarily sensory, altered chemosensory signaling during maturation could modulate neuro–glial communication required for AMso fate decisions. A missense change is a lower-probability indirect candidate [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: ugt-22 encodes a UDP-glycosyltransferase that can modulate receptor glycosylation and thus signaling; missense variants could subtly change surface receptor function on AMso or neighboring cells. This is a weak indirect mechanism by which MCM fate could be affected [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: ugt-22 is a glycosyltransferase predicted at membranes; glycosylation changes can alter receptor function and signaling relevant to cell fate. A missense change could subtly affect surface receptors in AMso and thereby the asymmetric division outcome [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: C01G6.5 is an uncharacterized gene with a missense change; lacking annotation reduces confidence, though perturbation of an uncharacterized neuronal/glial factor could conceivably interfere with AMso asymmetric division. This is a low-priority candidate pending expression or functional data [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: Uncharacterized gene with a missense variant; lack of annotation lowers prior probability, but any neuronal-expressed gene could influence local signaling or cytoskeleton of AMso, so it remains a weak candidate [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: ZK1067.2 is unannotated; the missense variant yields little mechanistic plausibility without further expression or functional data. I assign low causal probability unless follow-up shows expression in AMso or regulation of polarity/fate pathways [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: Uncharacterized missense; without functional annotation this is a low-priority candidate but could be retained for follow-up if other candidates are excluded [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: An upstream variant in brc-1 may alter regulatory control; BRCA1 orthologs have been linked to neuronal regeneration and signaling. While not an obvious primary candidate for AMso fate switching, altered DNA-repair or regulatory roles could indirectly affect cell divisions during maturation [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 33593852].
rationale: brc-1 functions in DNA repair and has reported roles in neuronal regeneration; upstream variant may have regulatory consequences but is low impact here. It remains a weak indirect candidate for affecting cell divisions during maturation [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; EMS=non-EMS; GeneRef: PMID 33593852].

Narrative: The upstream variant near cyd-1 (cyclin D) could modulate expression; CYD-1 is implicated in regulation of asymmetric protein localization and cell-cycle processes. Perturbed cyd-1 expression could change the cell-cycle dynamics of AMso and affect asymmetric division, offering a plausible albeit low-confidence mechanism [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: cyd-1 (cyclin D) is involved in cell-cycle control and asymmetric protein localization in cell fate determination; the variant is upstream (low impact) but cyd-1 dysfunction can alter division asymmetry—so regulatory changes could contribute to AMso symmetric divisions [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: M01E5.2 is predicted to be a mitochondrial GTPase involved in ribosome biogenesis; mitochondrial/ribosome defects can influence dividing cell competence. This missense allele is a low-priority indirect candidate for altering AMso division outcomes [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: M01E5.2 is a predicted GTPase (mitochondrial/ribosome biogenesis); defects in ribosome biogenesis can impair rapidly changing cells during maturation. A missense there is a low-probability indirect candidate for AMso division defects [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: ttn-1 is a large cytoskeletal (muscle) protein; while mainly muscle-expressed, major ECM/cytoskeletal changes can indirectly influence glial cell positioning. A missense here is a low-likelihood candidate for the MCM phenotype without supporting expression in head/glia [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: ttn-1 encodes a giant cytoskeletal/muscle protein; while primarily muscle-expressed, cytoskeletal regulators can influence extracellular architecture and indirectly affect glial positioning; missense impact is low-probability for MCM loss [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: M04F3.5 is predicted to bind actin and localize to filopodia and head neurons; missense variation could affect cell projections or local morphology. If AMso morphology or contacts are altered, division orientation and fate may change, but this is a speculative, low-confidence connection [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: M04F3.5 is predicted to bind actin and localize to filopodia and head neurons; perturbation could affect cell morphology or local signaling in AMso, modestly increasing chance of symmetric divisions leading to MCM absence [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: cutl-28 is predicted to be involved in morphogenesis and extracellular interactions; a missense variant could subtly alter extracellular/morphogen gradients that influence AMso behavior. This is a low-probability indirect mechanism for MCM loss absent further evidence [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: cutl-28 is predicted to participate in morphogenesis and extracellular interactions; a missense variant is a low-likelihood indirect candidate that could affect tissue architecture around AMso and influence division symmetry [Effect=missense_variant; EMS=non-EMS].

Narrative: II:10122829 C>T introduces a premature start gain in the 5' UTR of F27E5.7 (DUF2147 protein), potentially altering expression; regulatory impacts are uncertain. This variant is low-priority for MCM phenotype until functional or expression data indicate involvement in AMso or male maturation pathways [Effect=5_prime_UTR_premature_start_codon_gain_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
rationale: This 5' UTR premature start-gain variant could alter expression of a DUF-containing protein; regulatory effects are uncertain, so it is considered a low-probability candidate pending functional data [Effect=5_prime_UTR_premature_start_codon_gain_variant; EMS=non-EMS].
